anti_overlap: Focuses on multi-channel symbolic abstraction from dance notation, not compositional grammar (heraldry) or spatial importance (astronomy)
decision_lens: Asks 'what level of abstraction captures the movement without losing the choreographic intent?' — maps to 'what abstraction captures terminal state without losing agent-relevant information'
distance_rationale: Dance notation systems encode rich spatial-temporal data in compact symbolic marks — structurally isomorphic to terminal state encoding but from a completely unexpected domain.
expected_isomorphisms: Multi-channel separation (structure/content/emphasis), motif vs. full notation (summary vs. detail), and effort qualities (movement qualities to text styling) directly transfer.
focus: Dance notation systems — encoding complex spatial-temporal movement in compact symbolic marks
name: fd-choreographic-notation
persona: Choreographer and notation specialist versed in Labanotation and Benesh movement notation, who understands how to encode body positions, spatial paths, and timing in minimal symbolic marks on a staff
review_areas: Level of body representation — Labanotation distinguishes 'support', 'gesture', and 'body' columns. Terminal state could have 'structure', 'content', and 'emphasis' channels.
Direction symbols vs. position coordinates — notation uses 8 directional symbols instead of x,y coordinates. Terminal content could use relative positioning.
Effort notation — Laban's effort graph encodes quality-of-movement in 4 dimensions. Maps to: encoding emphasis quality (dim, bold, blinking, inverse).
Motif notation — simplified notation for choreographic intent vs. full notation for exact reproduction. Maps to: summary vs. full-fidelity terminal state.

severity_examples.condition: Agent must parse full terminal state when a high-level summary of changes would suffice
Can't separate 'what changed' from 'where everything is'
severity_examples.scenario: Temporal and spatial mixed in one encoding

source_domain: Choreographic notation (Labanotation, Benesh movement notation, 20th century)
success_hints: Proposes a multi-channel encoding where structure, content, and emphasis are separable layers
task_context: Dance notation compresses rich 3D spatial-temporal information into compact 2D symbolic marks. Terminal state is simpler (2D grid + attributes) but faces the same compression challenge.
